claims.text: Setting the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service lets Terraform and OpenTofu use the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud as a state backend.
PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN is the environment variable that specifies the domain serving the Terraform-compatible API in self-hosted Pulumi Cloud (for example `tf.pulumiapi.acmecorp.com`).
When PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN is unset, the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud Terraform-compatible API is disabled and its routes aren't registered.
The DNS record for the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN domain should point at the same host that serves PULUMI_API_DOMAIN in self-hosted Pulumi Cloud.
PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN can be set to the same value as PULUMI_API_DOMAIN in self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, so a separate domain or second DNS record is not required.

The Pulumi state backend guide at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ uses `tf.pulumi.com` as the domain in the Terraform/OpenTofu configuration, the `terraform login` or `tofu login` command, and the `TF_TOKEN_*` variable name.
A page exists at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ documenting the Pulumi Cloud Terraform state backend.
